title: Refinement
description: One change made in response to findings, recorded against what it closes so the next run can ask whether it held. A refinement with check.kind=none is legal and closes nothing: a class fixed with a paragraph is not closed, it is untested.

rung.description: R1 prose · R2 worked example · R3 script or test · R4 connector gate · R5 schema constraint. Higher depends on fewer people: R1/R2 depend on a reader, R3 on someone running it, R4/R5 on nothing. A recurrence lands STRICTLY above the rung its previous refinement landed on.

mode.description: detective means it finds the defect after the fact and raises a finding rather than preventing it. Legitimate only where prevention has a stated ceiling — and then the ceiling must be recorded too.

direction.description: widened is the correct response to a recurrence whose check existed and did not fire — a scope defect, usually one grain down. narrowed must carry a reason citing the authority order or an adjudication; a check narrowed to make a failure go away is a suppression, and this field is how a later run finds the moment the net got smaller.

kind.description: none means R1 or R2. A refinement with kind=none may not appear in a resolve_finding call.

id.description: Test node id, gate id, constraint name, or script entrypoint.

command.description: The exact command a later run can re-run.

output.description: The outcome line itself, not a description of it.

negative_control.description: Proof the check would have caught the defect. Required whenever this refinement is used to resolve anything. A check that passes on both the broken and the fixed state closes nothing and will be believed anyway.

method.description: How the broken state was reconstructed.

reference.description: The sha:path, fixture path, or payload id used.

failed_as_expected.description: false blocks the resolve. So does ran=false. There is no third option where you were confident.

output.description: The failure line the check produced on the broken state.

closes.description: Finding ids this refinement actually closes. Empty is legal and normal for R1/R2. One refinement closing six findings is the shape a structural change makes; six refinements closing one each is the shape a queue makes.

cluster_name.description: The class this answers, 12-30 words, stating the two points the defect lives between — e.g. 'validated at submit and discarded at promotion'. Where the two points are IS the choice of rung.

ceiling.description: Set when this class cannot be prevented above a certain rung — e.g. nothing downstream can distinguish a polled empty roster from an unpolled one. Naming the ceiling stops the next run from reading a recurrence as a rung-choice failure when it is a reachability limit.

reason.description: 15-40 words naming what this catch DEPENDS ON. 'Fires on every CI run, so it depends on CI running, which the nightly scanner guarantees.' That sentence is what the next run reads when deciding whether the rung held.

rung_not_reached.description: When the right rung was out of reach this run: the rung you could not reach and why. The class stays OPEN. Never let 'we did something' close it — a class closed at R2 when it needed R5 comes back looking like a new finding.

commit.description: The commit sha carrying this refinement.

session_ref.description: The session that made the change.
